headline: Reuters reports hackers accessed main US Air Force cloud platform
summary: Reuters reports that hackers got into the main cloud platform used by the US Air Force. The single-source summary does not say who the attackers were, how they got in, or how much data was affected.

headline: North Korea-linked PolinRider campaign plants Python loader in over 7,600 GitHub repositories
summary: SafeDep reports that the PolinRider campaign has hidden a Python loader in thousands of GitHub repositories, inside small utils packages or conftest.py files. The loader runs when the file is imported. It reportedly gets its next step from blockchain transaction data. The activity has been linked to North Korea and may date back to February 2025.
overrides: Global deployment applicability: every region 85%; cross-industry relevance at least 50%

headline: myColorado state digital ID app breach may affect about 100,000 users
summary: Attackers breached myColorado, Colorado's state digital identification and document storage app, and accessed data that users had uploaded. Around 100,000 people may be affected.

headline: SAP confirms GitHub intrusion; source code reportedly copied and altered using stolen tokens
summary: SAP detected suspicious activity on GitHub, where attackers reportedly used stolen employee tokens to copy and modify source code. Reports have not confirmed whether altered code reached customer releases.
overrides: Global deployment applicability: every region 85%; cross-industry relevance at least 50%

headline: SAP confirms cyber incident after reports its development infrastructure and source code were accessed
summary: SAP has confirmed a cybersecurity incident. It follows reports that attackers got into the company's software development infrastructure and may have accessed source code. It is not yet known whether customer-facing products or builds were affected.
overrides: Global deployment applicability: every region 85%; cross-industry relevance at least 50%

headline: UK DWP takes welfare and pension online services offline after cyber incident
summary: The UK Department for Work and Pensions took its online services offline as a precaution after a cyber incident. It says regular pension and benefit payments have not been affected. The nature and cause of the incident have not been disclosed.

headline: SAP confirms cybersecurity incident following Der Spiegel report
summary: SAP has confirmed it was recently hacked, a day after Der Spiegel reported the incident. The source does not say what was affected, whether customer data was involved, or whether any products were impacted.

headline: UK Department for Work and Pensions takes services offline after cyber incident
summary: The UK Department for Work and Pensions reported a cyber incident and took several services offline as a precaution. It has not disclosed the nature of the incident or whether any data was affected.

headline: Critical Linux kernel NFS server flaw (NFS2ROOT) could give remote attackers root access
summary: A critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel NFS server, tracked as CVE-2026-99362 and nicknamed NFS2ROOT, could let remote attackers gain root privileges. The bug is reported to be about 12 years old. The report does not mention active exploitation.

headline: Drupal warns a second critical site-takeover flaw is being exploited in attacks
summary: The Drupal security team says attackers are actively exploiting a second critical vulnerability, an access bypass that allows takeover of unpatched sites. No CVE identifier was given in the source.
overrides: No source-reported exploitation or recent KEV evidence; vulnerability capped at high

headline: SAP confirms security incident after detecting suspicious GitHub activity
summary: SAP confirmed it took urgent action to protect customers after detecting suspicious activity in its IT environment, linked to its GitHub presence. The scope and any customer impact have not been reported.
overrides: Global deployment applicability: every region 85%; cross-industry relevance at least 50%

headline: Swiss cyber agency confirms first AI-agent-assisted intrusions, including at critical infrastructure
summary: Switzerland's cybersecurity agency reported five confirmed attacks that used AI agents. Four of them succeeded, including two of the three that targeted critical infrastructure operators. No major disruption was reported, and the victims and attackers have not been identified.
overrides: No source-reported exploitation or recent KEV evidence; vulnerability capped at high

headline: 'GoodGuys' phishing campaign uses fake paid expert interviews to steal Google and Okta logins
summary: An ongoing phishing campaign called GoodGuys impersonates brands such as Google, Nvidia, Accenture and SpaceX. It sends fake invitations to paid expert interviews and webinars to harvest corporate Google and Okta credentials.

headline: Unpatched Cacti zero-day allows unauthenticated remote code execution; PoC published
summary: A researcher has published details and a proof-of-concept for an unpatched Cacti flaw, called 4HTTP2SHELL/4HTTP2ROOT. Starting from guest access, it reaches command execution in four HTTP requests. No CVE has been assigned yet, and no exploitation in the wild has been reported.

headline: Hex package manager discloses web server command-execution flaw and possible data exposure
summary: A flaw in hex.pm, the Elixir/Erlang package registry, allowed attackers to run commands on its web servers. Hex found no evidence that data was modified, but database reads are not logged, so data exposure cannot be ruled out.

headline: US DOJ announces its largest crackdown on scam rings, reporting nearly $17 billion seized
summary: The US Justice Department says it has acted against more than 800 alleged scammers in over 400 cases across 85 federal districts, with 30 defendants extradited. US agents joined police in more than 10 countries to raid overseas scam call centers and compounds.

headline: Official Q-Dir and DesktopOK installers and updates trojanized to deliver remote access malware
summary: Researchers report a supply-chain attack that tampered with Q-Dir and DesktopOK installation files distributed from the official SoftwareOK website. Evidence suggests malicious files were served both on direct download and during updates of existing installations, delivering remote access malware.

headline: Microsoft releases out-of-band hotpatch to fix Windows Server 2025 crashes caused by KB5131077
summary: Microsoft has released an emergency hotpatch for Windows Server 2025. It fixes crashes that started after this month's security hotpatch, KB5131077, was installed. The issue is about stability, not a security exploit.

headline: Microsoft to remove WSUS server role from Windows Server 2028
summary: Microsoft will drop the Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) role from Windows Server 2028, its next major server release. Organizations that rely on WSUS to distribute patches will need to plan a move to other update-management tools.

headline: Dutch NCSC warns of risks as business AI adoption rises
summary: The Dutch NCSC has warned about the security risks of AI, responding to Statistics Netherlands (CBS) figures showing more businesses are using it. This is guidance only; the source summary does not describe any new obligations.

headline: Microsoft: Chinese and North Korean state actors using ARTEX LLM-driven pentest framework
summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports that state-sponsored groups linked to China and North Korea are now using ARTEX in attacks. ARTEX is an open-source penetration testing framework, published on GitHub in July 2026, in which AI agents plan and carry out the steps needed to reach an operator-set goal. The source does not name specific victims or sectors.

headline: Germany's BSI warns of growing threat from autonomously operating AI
summary: Germany's federal cybersecurity agency, the BSI, has warned of a growing threat from AI systems that operate autonomously. The excerpt does not include specific incidents or technical details.

headline: Microsoft Store app used to deliver Vinci RAT via fake snipping tool site
summary: eSentire describes an intrusion chain that begins with a redirect to a fake snipping-tool website. From there, victims receive a Microsoft-signed installer tied to a Microsoft Store app, which then drops the Vinci remote access trojan. Abusing a trusted distribution channel can get around controls that rely on reputation.

headline: Japan's education ministry discloses breach of government procurement system
summary: Japan's education ministry said hackers breached its government procurement system. Records containing business information and email addresses may have been exposed.

headline: Remus infostealer uses fake Google Sheets Chrome extension to steal Gmail messages
summary: The Remus infostealer uses a malicious Chrome extension that poses as Google Sheets to steal Gmail messages. Its operators advertised this as a Gmail zero-day, but the report describes it as extension abuse rather than a flaw in Gmail.

headline: CVE-2026-40558: Perl Net::FTP flaw lets malicious FTP servers redirect passive-mode data connections
summary: A flaw in Perl's libnet Net::FTP module lets a malicious FTP server redirect a client's passive-mode data connection to an arbitrary third-party host. Net::FTP ships with Perl, and libnet v3.17 includes a fix. Amazon Linux's record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available.

headline: Flight Centre reports breach of third-party accommodation booking system exposing some passport details
summary: Flight Centre Travel Group told the Australian Securities Exchange that it is investigating unusual activity in a third-party accommodation booking system used by several of its brands. Customer names were accessed, and in rare cases passport and health details. The company says flight bookings were treated separately from the affected system.

headline: US recovery firm CEO charged with defrauding ransomware victims
summary: US authorities have charged the founder and CEO of a US data recovery company with defrauding companies that had been hit by ransomware. The short source report gives few details about the alleged scheme.

headline: Kaspersky reports rise in Android devices shipped with preinstalled malware
summary: Kaspersky says the number of Android devices that arrive with malware already installed has risen sharply. The source excerpt does not name device models, malware families or affected regions.

headline: FIFA confirms breach exposing limited personal and business data
summary: FIFA, which is based in Zurich, has confirmed that attackers accessed a limited set of personal and business information and that some of it was published. It has not said when the attack happened or what data was taken, and it is working with law enforcement.

headline: FIFA confirms cyberattack exposed limited personal and business information
summary: FIFA has confirmed that a cyberattack exposed a limited set of personal and business information. The source does not describe the attack method, who was responsible or how many people were affected.

headline: FIFA discloses cyberattack that accessed personal and business information
summary: FIFA says attackers accessed personal and business information in a cyberattack. The organization has not said when the attack happened or exactly what data was affected.

headline: Cyberattack forces AFP to take global news distribution platform offline
summary: Agence France-Presse was hit by a cyberattack and took one of its main news distribution platforms offline. The platform delivers content to media organizations worldwide. No attacker, method or data impact has been reported.

headline: CREST study finds most threat-led penetration testing providers now use AI
summary: CREST research based on 26 providers found that 81% use AI in threat-led penetration testing beyond the experimental stage. The study focuses on financial services and raises questions about control of AI and how much assurance AI-assisted testing really provides.

headline: SailPoint predicts accountability pressure on AI agent identities in 2027
summary: SailPoint's predictions report expects regulators, boards and insurers to demand governance of autonomous AI agents. Its research says 79% of enterprises run AI agents in production, but only 2% have identity controls designed for them.

headline: Bits of Freedom criticises Dutch data protection authority as a failing regulator
summary: The Dutch civil rights group Bits of Freedom has again criticised the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, calling it a failing regulator. The criticism concerns how privacy oversight is enforced in the Netherlands.

headline: Opinion: security metrics should reflect current exposure, not quarterly reporting
summary: This opinion piece argues that many security metrics are assembled for presentations rather than for running operations. It calls for continuously updated measures of exposure as attackers move faster.

headline: Weekly roundup: tanker cyberattacks, EU Quantum Act, USDA payment breach, Radware hack
summary: This SecurityWeek roundup briefly covers several items: cyberattacks on tankers, an EU Quantum Act, new VirusTotal capabilities and a breach of USDA payment systems. It also reports that security firm Radware was hacked and that RansomwareHelp has been accused of profiting from ransom payments. Few details are given for any item.

headline: Schneier: recent US outages are unrelated and rooted in underinvestment, not cyberattacks
summary: Bruce Schneier argues that recent outages were coincidences, not a coordinated attack. The affected organisations include Microsoft, the FAA, several banks, United Airlines, Apple and a classified NSA network. He links these failures to economic incentives that leave infrastructure underfunded.

headline: Weekly roundup: NGINX exposure, malicious browser extensions and AI server hijacking
summary: This weekly recap covers about 20 stories. They include roughly 10 million NGINX services reportedly at risk, more than 250 malicious browser extensions and the hijacking of AI servers. The source excerpt does not give technical specifics.

headline: Stolen iPhone used for more than €22,000 in fraudulent payment transactions
summary: A thief used a stolen iPhone to make more than €22,000 in fraudulent payment transactions. Security.NL reported the case, which was most likely in the Netherlands. It shows the risk of account takeover through stolen mobile devices.

headline: Creator pulls open-source CyberStrikeAI offensive framework; enterprise version still available
summary: The open-source version of CyberStrikeAI, an AI-driven pentesting framework, has been permanently removed by its creator. An enterprise version of the tool is still available.

headline: Norton launches scam-detection connector for Claude chatbot users
summary: Norton released a connector that brings its Genie AI scam-detection features into Claude. Users can submit suspicious messages, screenshots and links for analysis, and the connector does not require a Norton account. This is a consumer product showcase.

headline: Paper password notebooks reportedly gaining popularity in Japan amid data leaks
summary: Security.NL reports that sales of paper notebooks for writing down login credentials are rising in Japan. The reported reason is the growing number of data leaks. This is a consumer-behaviour story with no direct operational impact on enterprises.

headline: OpenAI fixes GPT-6.2 usage-metering bug, so users will hit usage limits faster
summary: OpenAI fixed a bug that had wrongly discounted GPT-6.2 usage. As a result, users will reach usage limits about 40% sooner than before. This is a billing change, not a security issue.

headline: Essay quote criticises homogenised AI-generated content
summary: A blog post quotes an essay arguing that AI-generated text from Claude is making videos, talks and email pitches sound alike. It is commentary and contains no security incident or vulnerability.

headline: Malwarebytes offers Black Friday discount on consumer security subscriptions
summary: Malwarebytes is running a 50% Black Friday discount on its consumer and small-business security products. This is a promotion with no threat content.

headline: NordVPN Black Friday promotion
summary: This is a commercial VPN discount promotion. It contains no security-relevant event.
